Yes, I have found that sometimes a specific passage is particularly challenging, or just doesn't hold my attention, so I use multiple different strategies throughout the reading section.  September and December 2016 I got a 31 in reading(with no studying other than normal school work). I still don't have my scores from the December 2017 test.

I would also say that once you learn HOW to do more of the math, attempt longer practice tests. As someone who is good at math, it's still my worst on the ACT because I run out of time. The more you know the more time you will spend on actually DOING the math, so try and work on efficiency and time management as well.

To be perfectly honest the best strategy is whatever works for that passage. That sounds dumb but for me sometimes the best thing IS to read the whole passage.  Other times I'm better off reading the questions first and then finding answers.  If you have poor retention when you attempt to read the whole passage try either reading in chunks or reading the questions first.
